name: island-archipelago
title: Carrying capacity sets abundance, not richness
question:
In the Lotka-Volterra island model, does island area control the equilibrium
state — and if so, which quantity: total abundance, species richness, or both?
hypothesis:
Area enters the model only through the carrying capacity
(max_individuals_capacity = area * individuals_per_area), which caps TOTAL
individuals. With a random (non-trophic) interaction matrix, Lotka-Volterra
competition drives strong competitive exclusion on every island regardless of
size, so equilibrium TOTAL ABUNDANCE should scale tightly with area while
equilibrium SPECIES RICHNESS should be low and essentially independent of area
— i.e. this model does NOT reproduce the classic MacArthur-Wilson species-area
law under random competition.
objective:
Run the `island_archipelago` composite (a mainland + 5 smaller islands, each
an IslandProcess coupled by one MigrationProcess) to equilibrium and measure,
across islands, the correlation of (a) equilibrium total abundance with area
and (b) equilibrium species richness with log-area.
description:
Faithful port of experiments/island_lotka_volterra.py. Area appears only as
the per-island carrying capacity in the discrete LV update's rescale step.
The study separates the two things "area effect" could mean and shows the
model couples area to abundance (exactly) but not to richness (random
competition collapses each island to a couple of dominant species). Study 3
(island-food-web) shows that trophic interaction structure is what restores
the area-richness relationship.

expected_behavior.name: abundance-scales-with-area
expected_behavior.en:
Across islands, equilibrium TOTAL abundance is near-perfectly correlated
with island area — each island fills to its carrying capacity.
expected_behavior.rationale:
Area enters the LV update only as the carrying-capacity cap
(area * individuals_per_area); dominant species grow until the island's
projected total is rescaled to that cap, so equilibrium total tracks area
almost exactly (measured corr ~ 1.00).

expected_behavior.name: richness-not-set-by-area
expected_behavior.en:
Across islands, equilibrium species richness is NOT positively driven by
area under random competition: the richness-vs-log-area correlation stays
below 0.35 (measured ~ -0.10).
expected_behavior.rationale:
Random Lotka-Volterra competition causes strong competitive exclusion
independent of capacity, so bigger islands hold more individuals of the same
few winners rather than more species. This is the honest divergence from
classic MacArthur-Wilson theory — area sets abundance, not diversity, when
interactions are non-trophic. (Contrast Study 3.)

behavior_tests.name: abundance-scales-with-area
behavior_tests.description: Pearson corr of per-island equilibrium total abundance vs area must exceed 0.95.

provenance.note:
Carrying capacity is area * individuals_per_area and the LV rescale
drives each island's total to that cap; the ~1.00 correlation is a
direct, near-deterministic consequence of the ported update rule.

behavior_tests.name: richness-not-set-by-area
behavior_tests.description: Pearson corr of per-island equilibrium richness vs log-area must stay below 0.35.

provenance.note:
Measured richness-vs-log-area corr under random competition is ~ -0.10
(6-island, 30-species, seed 0, equilibrium tail); 0.35 is a generous
ceiling that still fails loudly if a strong positive species-area law
appeared, which it does not for non-trophic interactions.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
island-archipelago establishes the carrying-capacity baseline and the
"no species-area law under random competition" result that island-food-web
is contrasted against.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Lotka-Volterra archipelago (6 islands, 30 species, 150 generations, seed 0)
